data.narrative:
Enapter is a publicly listed Climate & Energy company trading on Frankfurt (ticker H2O). The valuation universe for this sector comprises nine peers across public and private markets: one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private-stage companies including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient clustering by stage, valuation tier, or business model similarity to support a robust peer-median approach.

Peer-median triangulation is inapplicable here. While nine same-sector peers exist, filtering by stage proximity, valuation tier, and business comparability yields fewer than the three minimum datapoints required for statistical reliability. A cross-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of Climate & Energy business models, capital intensity, and development timelines. The public comp (LNZA) represents a single datapoint and cannot anchor a range independently.

Without sufficient narrow-peer density or disclosed comparable transaction data in the filing, this analysis cannot produce a supported valuation range. The key uncertainty is stage-appropriate peer definition: Enapter's position as a publicly listed, operationalized hydrogen electrolyzer manufacturer may differ materially from the mix of early-stage materials science, energy storage, and metals recycling businesses in the peer universe. Additional disclosure of revenue multiples, EBITDA margins, or capex intensity would be required to establish a defensible triangulated valuation.
